# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

The AGENTS.md is long. Let me continue reading it to find relevant info, and also look at GOAL.md. But first, the key focus areas for this ticket:

1. `_switchToMetadata` in `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` — switch double-pays the boot
2. Shell boot ~4s
3. Context build ~2s — cacheable per (session, lastRecordId)

Acceptance:
- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep behavior + tests stay green

Related: #1728 (the switch lease race — same machinery; fixing the double-pay touches the same code and should land after/with it).

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow
    detection via error-message regexes.
  - **Invariant to preserve: providers never throw.** All failures —
    network, 429, abort, malformed SSE — arrive as an `error` event with
    `stopReason: error|aborted`. The agent loop never sees an exception from
    a provider.
- `packages/agent/` (~8.1k LOC TS):
  - `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` (748 LOC) — the low-level async loop;
    port its shape, not its incidental JS-isms.
  - `packages/agent/src/agent.ts` (557 LOC) — stateful `Agent` with
    **steering / follow-up queues** (inject user messages mid-run — this is
    first-class behavior we must keep) and hooks (`beforeToolCall`,
    `afterToolCall`, `transformContext`, `prepareNextTurn`).
  - session layer — sessions as an **append-only JSONL tree** of records
    (branching, labels). Flat linear history is not acceptable.
  - compaction pipeline (~760 LOC) — `estimateTokens` (chars/4 heuristic,
    images ≈ 1200 tokens) → `shouldCompact` (reserve 16384 tokens) →
    `findCutPoint` (keep ~20k recent tokens) → `generateSummary` via LLM with
    a fixed structured prompt. Token-based, never message-count-based.
  - `ExecutionEnv` abstraction (FileSystem + Shell) — our portability
    boundary: default implementation uses `dart:io`, a web implementation

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow
    detection via error-message regexes.
  - **Invariant to preserve: providers never throw.** All failures —
    network, 429, abort, malformed SSE — arrive as an `error` event with
    `stopReason: error|aborted`. The agent loop never sees an exception from
    a provider.
- `packages/agent/` (~8.1k LOC TS):
  - `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` (748 LOC) — the low-level async loop;
    port its shape, not its incidental JS-isms.
  - `packages/agent/src/agent.ts` (557 LOC) — stateful `Agent` with
    **steering / follow-up queues** (inject user messages mid-run — this is
    first-class behavior we must keep) and hooks (`beforeToolCall`,
    `afterToolCall`, `transformContext`, `prepareNextTurn`).
  - session layer — sessions as an **append-only JSONL tree** of records
    (branching, labels). Flat linear history is not acceptable.
  - compaction pipeline (~760 LOC) — `estimateTokens` (chars/4 heuristic,
    images ≈ 1200 tokens) → `shouldCompact` (reserve 16384 tokens) →
    `findCutPoint` (keep ~20k recent tokens) → `generateSummary` via LLM with
    a fixed structured prompt. Token-based, never message-count-based.
  - `ExecutionEnv` abstraction (FileSystem + Shell) — our portability
    boundary: default implementation uses `dart:io`, a web implementation

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.

# GOAL — flutter_agent_harness

## Objective

Build the **ideal cross-platform AI agent harness in Dart**, ported from the
architecture of **pi-mono** (`packages/ai` + `packages/agent`), publishable on
pub.dev and runnable everywhere Dart runs: **VM, Flutter desktop, iOS/Android,
and web**. The core package must stay **pure Dart** — no `dart:io`, no Flutter
imports in `lib/` (platform specifics live behind abstractions).

This repo is the successor to the adk_dart-based assistant stack in the
`yoclip` project; once mature it will power the yoclip Studio AI assistant.

## Reference codebases (read these first)

### Primary architecture reference — pi-mono

`/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/references/pi/`

- `packages/ai/` (~8.7k LOC TS) — provider adapters behind one contract:
  `stream(model, context, options) → AssistantMessageEventStream`.
  Study these files before writing any provider code:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` (~1205 LOC) — the
    canonical adapter; also covers OpenRouter (`baseUrl` swap, first-class).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (~1242 LOC) — includes a
    hand-rolled SSE decoder at lines 260–409; port this to Dart.
  - `packages/ai/src/stream.ts` — event contract:
    `start → text/thinking/toolcall_{start,delta,end} → done|error`, every
    delta event carries the **live partial message** (partial-first design).
  - `packages/ai/src/utils/overflow.ts` — provider-specific context-overflow
    detection via error-message regexes.
  - **Invariant to preserve: providers never throw.** All failures —
    network, 429, abort, malformed SSE — arrive as an `error` event with
    `stopReason: error|aborted`. The agent loop never sees an exception from
    a provider.
- `packages/agent/` (~8.1k LOC TS):
  - `packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts` (748 LOC) — the low-level async loop;
    port its shape, not its incidental JS-isms.
  - `packages/agent/src/agent.ts` (557 LOC) — stateful `Agent` with
    **steering / follow-up queues** (inject user messages mid-run — this is
    first-class behavior we must keep) and hooks (`beforeToolCall`,
    `afterToolCall`, `transformContext`, `prepareNextTurn`).
  - session layer — sessions as an **append-only JSONL tree** of records
    (branching, labels). Flat linear history is not acceptable.
  - compaction pipeline (~760 LOC) — `estimateTokens` (chars/4 heuristic,
    images ≈ 1200 tokens) → `shouldCompact` (reserve 16384 tokens) →
    `findCutPoint` (keep ~20k recent tokens) → `generateSummary` via LLM with
    a fixed structured prompt. Token-based, never message-count-based.
  - `ExecutionEnv` abstraction (FileSystem + Shell) — our portability
    boundary: default implementation uses `dart:io`, a web implementation

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.

Now let me understand the ticket more deeply. The ticket is about performance:

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId).

Acceptance criteria:
- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

Let me check related tickets: #1728 (the switch lease race), #1726, #1729, #155.

Make `/sessions` switch not re-boot the shell stack — i.e., `_switchToMetadata` should NOT re-run `_loadAgentContext()` etc. Wait, actually the ticket says config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. That's needed when cwd changes. But `_loadAgentContext()` reloads skills/project context — how expensive is that?

So the "double pay" is that booting `fa` first creates/opens a default session (which for `--session name` wouldn't happen — the named session is loaded directly), and then the switch re-runs the whole session lifecycle on top.

So the fix for root cause 1: when the user picks a session via `/sessions`, we can't avoid the initial default boot (they typed `fa` before knowing which session). But we CAN make sure the switch itself doesn't redo things that are already live. Actually wait, more precisely:

For `fa --session goal_builder` (~6s): session open 70ms + context build ~200ms + shell boot ~350-400ms. So even the direct named-session start pays a 2s context build and ~4s shell boot.

For `fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder (~12s): pays full boot twice — shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (1839ms) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

Could be skipped when cwd unchanged (it's already conditioned on cwd change inside `_loadSessionInner`, but `_switchToMetadata` calls it BEFORE `_loadSession` unconditionally). Actually looking at the code: `_switchToMetadata` sets `_env.cwd = metadata.cwd` then calls `await _loadAgentContext()` unconditionally. Now let me understand the ticket more deeply. The ticket is about performance:

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId).

Acceptance criteria:
- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

Now let me understand the acceptance criteria again and decide the implementation plan. The ticket says:

**Root cause 1**: Switch double-pays the boot (`_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.

Hmm, what does `_switchToMetadata` do that "re-bots the shell stack"? Actually, looking closely — it calls `_loadAgentContext()` which reloads:
- `loadPromptTemplates`
- `_reloadSkills()` — full skill discovery
- `_detectThirdPartySkillDirs()`
- `loadProjectContextFiles()`
- `_applyPromptComposition()`
- `_refreshMemorySection()` (async)

When the cwd is the SAME (switching sessions in the same project), all this is identical work. The ticket says "no re-boot of the shell stack" for the mid-REPL switch acceptance. So the fix: skip `_loadAgentContext()` (and `builtInAgentModes` rebuild) when `_env.cwd == metadata.cwd` — the context is already live.

But wait — how much time does that save? The ticket's measurements: switch = open (66ms) + context build (1839ms) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s). And total switch ~12s - 6s boot = ~6s. So where are the other ~4s? config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are "already live" — the claim is the switch re-runs them? Hmm, let me re-read:

"**Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s."

So the current behavior: `fa` (default boot ~6s) + switch (~6s: open 66ms + context 1839ms + lease + rehydrate + replay ~2s). Hmm, 66+1839+200 = ~3.9s. The remaining ~2s could be `_loadAgentContext` (skills scan, project context, prompt build) + memory refresh etc.

The fix for root cause 1 in the switch path:
1. Skip `_loadAgentContext()` when the cwd hasn't changed (prompt/skills/project context already live).
2. Parallelize what can be parallelized (e.g., rehydrate can run parallel with replay).
3. Make the context build cached (root cause 3).

**Root cause 3**: Context build ~2s: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

So implement a context-build cache: key = (session path, lastRecordId), value = built `BuildContext`/messages. On `_loadSessionInner`, after `session.buildContext()`, cache the result. On a later open of the same session (mid-REPL switch back), if the file's last record id hasn't changed, reuse the cached messages.

How do we know the "lastRecordId" cheaply? Let me look at the Session API: `session.buildContext()`, `session.getMetadata()` has `lastUpdatedAt` maybe. Let me look at the windowed session storage to see what's available. Maybe there's a cheap way: file length + mtime? Or the session's `leafRecordId`?

**Acceptance: boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay)**. So add instrumentation: in `_switchToMetadata`, log `boot_stage switch-open/switch-walk/...`? Actually `_loadSessionInner`'s `stage()` already logs open/walk/context (for any load path, boot or switch). The missing ones: rehydrate (subagent) and replay (TUI history replay). So add `stage('rehydrate')` and `stage('replay')` in `_switchToMetadata`. Hmm wait — but the ticket says "currently switches log only `context`". Let me test that... Actually maybe there's a subtlety: `_logDiagnostic` in the switch path might fail? No wait — let me look again at `_loadSessionInner`'s stage function: it logs open, walk, context. The switch calls `_loadSession` → `_loadSessionInner`. So a switch logs open/walk/context already.

Hmm wait, let me re-read the ticket text: "boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`".

Maybe the author observed in the log that a switch emitted only `boot_stage context ms=1839` at 09:13:53. Because... maybe the open/walk lines were logged but with a different sid, or... Actually — WAIT. Let me look again at the `stage` closure: `_logDiagnostic('boot_stage $name ms=${bootSw.elapsedMilliseconds} sid=${metadata.id}')`. It logs open, walk, context. So switches DO log open/walk/context.

Hmm, unless the switch path doesn't go through `_loadSessionInner`... it does — `_switchToMetadata` calls `_loadSession(metadata)`.

Hmm, maybe the ticket author means: the log shows only `context` because open/walk are logged as `resume_timing` lines instead? Whatever — the acceptance is clear: make switch stage lines cover open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay. I'll add explicit switch-stage logging that names each stage of the switch lifecycle: open/walk/context (from the load), rehydrate, replay — plus maybe lease/model-restore stages. To be attributable, the lines should name the target session.

Let me now think about the **cold start** acceptance: `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s. Current: ~6s = 70ms open + ~2s context build + ~3.5-4s shell boot.

Shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init. That's in `bin/fah.dart` mostly (before `run()`), plus `run()`'s own pre-REPL stages. To hit ≤3s we need to cut ~3s. That's a lot. The ticket estimates "Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s" for root cause 2.

What can I actually do here in code:
- `acquirePowerAssertions()` — probably cheap.
- `_waiting.captureLostJobs()` — file IO, cheap.
- `_loadAgentContext()` — skills scan + project context files + prompt composition. This can be expensive (skills discovery scans directories). 
- `_loadPersistedModelCache()` — file read.
- `_initializeSession()` — for named session: `_sessionNameMatches` (repo list + sessionNamesQuick scan across all sessions!) + `_loadSession` (open 70ms + walk + context 2s + cap).

Note: `_sessionNameMatches` for a named boot scans ALL sessions' names (`sessionNamesQuick` fans out across every session file). On a big store that could be slow.

- `_claimSessionLease()`, `_registerLivePresence()`, `_subagentManager.rehydrate()`.
- TUI init.

Also before `run()`: bin/fah.dart does config parse, provider catalog, etc.

Honestly, hitting the ≤3s cold start depends on the machine and the 2.7GB session — I can't measure that here (I don't have the goal_builder session). What I CAN do:

1. Make the context build fast/cached so repeated opens are ~100ms.
2. Reduce redundant work in the switch path (skip `_loadAgentContext` when cwd unchanged).
3. Parallelize independent boot stages where safe.
4. Add the boot_stage instrumentation for switches.

Let me also check the context build path — `session.buildContext()` in the windowed storage. Let me read `windowed_session_storage.dart` and `session_storage.dart` around buildContext to see what's expensive and where a cache could hook.

The walk (`ensureCompactionBoundaryResident`) matters for the context correctness, but if the file hasn't changed, the previous walk landed the same residency. But the new Session instance starts fresh (open reads tail chunk only) — its resident window is the tail chunk; the walk then pages back to the boundary. If I skip the walk, `getPathToRoot` stops at the window edge and the built context would be truncated. So I can't skip the walk if I still open a fresh instance.

```dart

### Test 2: `test/session/custom_record_scan_memo_test.dart`

```dart
class CountingEnv extends MemoryExecutionEnv {

The 're-remembering the same path refreshes the entry' test failed — and it's flaky (passed in the earlier list run? It failed in both runs of the dir run, and now in isolation too). Line 88: `expect((hit!.messages.single as UserMessage).content, 'new')` — hit is null.

Why? `remember('/s/a.jsonl', 10,1,'old')` then `remember('/s/a.jsonl', 20,2,'new')`, then `match('/s/a.jsonl', 10,1)` → should MISS (entry replaced) → then `match(20,2)` → hit 'new'.

In my `match()`: entry exists ('new', 20,2); stats (10,1) mismatch → REMOVE the entry and return null. Then match(20,2) → entry GONE → null! 

The mismatch-removal is wrong: a miss with old stats shouldn't evict the entry — the entry describes a NEWER state; the probe is just stale. Fix `match()`: on mismatch, return null WITHOUT removing (keep the entry). Hmm — but then a path that was never remembered... can't be in the map. The eviction on mismatch was my design choice; removing it is safe: entries only leave via capacity LRU or re-remember. Actually wait — think about CLI behavior: match(path, stale-stats) returns null → rebuild → remember fresh → entry replaced anyway. Keeping the no-remove semantics is strictly better.

Update the implementation AND the test expectation stays as written (match(10,1) null; match(20,2) hit).

blocks.text:
The 're-remembering the same path refreshes the entry' test failed — and it's flaky (passed in the earlier list run? It failed in both runs of the dir run, and now in isolation too). Line 88: `expect((hit!.messages.single as UserMessage).content, 'new')` — hit is null.

Why? `remember('/s/a.jsonl', 10,1,'old')` then `remember('/s/a.jsonl', 20,2,'new')`, then `match('/s/a.jsonl', 10,1)` → should MISS (entry replaced) → then `match(20,2)` → hit 'new'.

In my `match()`: entry exists ('new', 20,2); stats (10,1) mismatch → REMOVE the entry and return null. Then match(20,2) → entry GONE → null! 

The mismatch-removal is wrong: a miss with old stats shouldn't evict the entry — the entry describes a NEWER state; the probe is just stale. Fix `match()`: on mismatch, return null WITHOUT removing (keep the entry). Hmm — but then a path that was never remembered... can't be in the map. The eviction on mismatch was my design choice; removing it is safe: entries only leave via capacity LRU or re-remember. Actually wait — think about CLI behavior: match(path, stale-stats) returns null → rebuild → remember fresh → entry replaced anyway. Keeping the no-remove semantics is strictly better.

Update the implementation AND the test expectation stays as written (match(10,1) null; match(20,2) hit).

Fix `match()`: on mismatch, return null WITHOUT removing (keep the entry). Hmm — but then a path that was never remembered... can't be in the map. The eviction on mismatch was my design choice; removing it is safe: entries only leave via capacity LRU or re-remember. Actually wait — think about CLI behavior: match(path, stale-stats) returns null → rebuild → remember fresh → entry replaced anyway. Keeping the no-remove semantics is strictly better.

The 're-remembering the same path refreshes the entry' test failed — and it's flaky (passed in the earlier list run? It failed in both runs of the dir run, and now in isolation too). Line 88: `expect((hit!.messages.single as UserMessage).content, 'new')` — hit is null.

Why? `remember('/s/a.jsonl', 10,1,'old')` then `remember('/s/a.jsonl', 20,2,'new')`, then `match('/s/a.jsonl', 10,1)` → should MISS (entry replaced) → then `match(20,2)` → hit 'new'.

In my `match()`: entry exists ('new', 20,2); stats (10,1) mismatch → REMOVE the entry and return null. Then match(20,2) → entry GONE → null! 

The mismatch-removal is wrong: a miss with old stats shouldn't evict the entry — the entry describes a NEWER state; the probe is just stale. Fix `match()`: on mismatch, return null WITHOUT removing (keep the entry). Hmm — but then a path that was never remembered... can't be in the map. The eviction on mismatch was my design choice; removing it is safe: entries only leave via capacity LRU or re-remember. Actually wait — think about CLI behavior: match(path, stale-stats) returns null → rebuild → remember fresh → entry replaced anyway. Keeping the no-remove semantics is strictly better.

The cache didn't hit. Why? In the test, alpha was boted via `--session alpha`? NO — I boot with NO sessionName: the CLI creates a default session. Alpha is NEVER loaded at boot! So the switch to alpha is a COLD load → no cache → then... wait, my test says "alpha was opened at boot" — but it wasn't! My test flow: boot default → `/session beta` (cold) → `/session $alphaId` (cold — first alpha load!). So no cache hit. The test comment is wrong.

### What changed
Mid-REPL `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack and warm switches reuse the built context: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd differs, `Session.buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) and reused when the file is unchanged, and the repo's custom-record tail scans (obligations ledger, orphan reports, subagent registry, steering) are memoized per (path, params, fingerprint). ### Key decisions
- Context cache keys on the file's stat fingerprint (size+mtime, probed before and after the open) — any append/rotation invalidates it without write-barier machinery; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.

Why? `remember('/s/a.jsonl', 10,1,'old')` then `remember('/s/a.jsonl', 20,2,'new')`, then `match('/s/a.jsonl', 10,1)` → should MISS (entry replaced) → then `match(20,2)` → hit 'new'.

In my `match()`: entry exists ('new', 20,2); stats (10,1) mismatch → REMOVE the entry and return null. Then match(20,2) → entry GONE → null!

The eviction on mismatch was my design choice; removing it is safe: entries only leave via capacity LRU or re-remember. ### What changed
Mid-REPL `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack and warm switches reuse the built context: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd differs, `Session.buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) and reused when the file is unchanged, and the repo's custom-record tail scans (obligations ledger, orphan reports, subagent registry, steering) are memoized per (path, params, fingerprint). Switches now log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage (switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done).

### Key decisions
- Context cache keys on the file's stat fingerprint (size+mtime, probed before and after the open) — any append/rotation invalidates it without write-barier machinery; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The context stage reports `source=cache` in fa.log so warm vs cold opens are attributable (gh-1734 AC: regressions attributable from the log).
- Scan memo returns shared immutable records (all consumers are read-only) — one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Same-cwd switch keeps the live prompt (skills/project-context rescan is skipped); a different-cwd switch still reloads, so the prompt always matches the session's project.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/cli/session_switch_boot_stages_test.dart \

arguments.content:
### What changed
- `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).
- Warm switches reuse the built context: `buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) in `ResumedContextCache`; an unchanged session file skips the projection walk entirely (`boot_stage context … source=cache` in fa.log).
- `JsonlSessionRepo.readCustomRecordsOfType` memoizes tail scans per (path, params, chain fingerprint) — the obligations-ledger/orphan-report/registry/steering rescans on every open/switch collapse to one stat each.
- Switches log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage — switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done, all naming the target sid — so regressions are attributable from fa.log alone.

### Key decisions
- Cache key = file stat fingerprint (probed before AND after the open): any append/rotation/truncate misses; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The memo returns shared immutable records (every consumer is read-only); one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Cold-boot cost is untouched by design — the remaining shell-boot work (config/providers/MCP/plugins) needs the lazy/parallel regime and stays measurable via the new stage lines.

### How to verify
```bash

```

{"content":"### What changed
- `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).
- Warm switches reuse the built context: `buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) in `ResumedContextCache`; an unchanged session file skips the projection walk entirely (`boot_stage context … source=cache` in fa.log).
- `JsonlSessionRepo.readCustomRecordsOfType` memoizes tail scans per (path, params, chain fingerprint) — the obligations-ledger/orphan-report/registry/steering rescans on every open/switch collapse to one stat each.
- Switches log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage — switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done, all naming the target sid — so regressions are attributable from fa.log alone.

### Key decisions
- Cache key = file stat fingerprint (probed before AND after the open): any append/rotation/truncate misses; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The memo returns shared immutable records (every consumer is read-only); one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Cold-boot cost is untouched by design — the remaining shell-boot work (config/providers/MCP/plugins) needs the lazy/parallel regime and stays measurable via the new stage lines.

```bash
dart test test/cli/session_switch_boot_stages_test.dart \

  REUSE --> REH[rehydrate · memoized scan]

### What changed
Mid-REPL `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack and warm switches reuse the built context: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd differs, `Session.buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) and reused when the file is unchanged, and the repo's custom-record tail scans (obligations ledger, orphan reports, subagent registry, steering) are memoized per (path, params, fingerprint). - Context cache keys on the file's stat fingerprint (size+mtime, probed before and after the open) — any append/rotation invalidates it without write-barier machinery; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The context stage reports `source=cache` in fa.log so warm vs cold opens are attributable (gh-1734 AC: regressions attributable from the log).
- Scan memo returns shared immutable records (all consumers are read-only) — one entry per session path bounds memory.

``

</details>
``

Mid-REPL `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack and warm switches reuse the built context: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd differs, `Session.buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) and reused when the file is unchanged, and the repo's custom-record tail scans (obligations ledger, orphan reports, subagent registry, steering) are memoized per (path, params, fingerprint). ### What changed
Mid-REPL `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack and warm switches reuse the built context: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd differs, `Session.buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) and reused when the file is unchanged, and the repo's custom-record tail scans (obligations ledger, orphan reports, subagent registry, steering) are memoized per (path, params, fingerprint). - Context cache keys on the file's stat fingerprint (size+mtime, probed before and after the open) — any append/rotation invalidates it without write-barier machinery; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The context stage reports `source=cache` in fa.log so warm vs cold opens are attributable (gh-1734 AC: regressions attributable from the log).
- Scan memo returns shared immutable records (all consumers are read-only) — one entry per session path bounds memory.

</details>

Could I make ONE scan serve multiple type sets? That's a bigger refactor of the memo (index multiple type-sets into one scan). 

Hmm — actually there IS a clean way: memoize at the FILE level with a per-scan type-UNION? No — keep scope. 

Alternative cheap win for cold start: the orphan seed uses `lastSegmentOnly: true` — already bounded. The obligations ledger inside buildContext scans the FULL chain (all segments, each capped 95MB) — on a rotated session that's segmentN * 95MB... The CLI's `_latestObligationsFromScan` (writer rehydrate, at first drive — off boot). buildContext's scan is the boot one.

mtime granularity on real FS: append within the same mtime tick changes SIZE — fingerprint includes size. Two appends of equal total size with same ms mtime — virtually impossible (appends strictly grow). Rotation: primary shrinks. ✔

```markdown
### What changed
Mid-REPL `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack and warm switches reuse the built context: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd differs, `Session.buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) and reused when the file is unchanged, and the repo's custom-record tail scans (obligations ledger, orphan reports, subagent registry, steering) are memoized per (path, params, fingerprint). Switches now log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage (switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done).

### Key decisions
- Context cache keys on the file's stat fingerprint (size+mtime, probed before and after the open) — any append/rotation invalidates it without write-barier machinery; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The context stage reports `source=cache` in fa.log so warm vs cold opens are attributable (gh-1734 AC: regressions attributable from the log).
- Scan memo returns shared immutable records (all consumers are read-only) — one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Same-cwd switch keeps the live prompt (skills/project-context rescan is skipped); a different-cwd switch still reloads, so the prompt always matches the session's project.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test/cli/session_switch_boot_stages_test.dart \
 test/cli/session_switch_prompt_reuse_test.dart \
 test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart \
 test/session/custom_record_scan_memo_test.dart
``
Then: `fa --session <big>`, `/sessions` → another session → back; fa.log shows `boot_stage context … source=cache` on the return switch.

<details><summary>Switch pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD

 LOAD --> CTX{context cache hit?}

{"content":"### What changed
- `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).
- Warm switches reuse the built context: `buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) in `ResumedContextCache`; an unchanged session file skips the projection walk entirely (`boot_stage context … source=cache` in fa.log).
- `JsonlSessionRepo.readCustomRecordsOfType` memoizes tail scans per (path, params, chain fingerprint) — the obligations-ledger/orphan-report/registry/steering rescans on every open/switch collapse to one stat each.
- Switches log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage — switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done, all naming the target sid — so regressions are attributable from fa.log alone.

### Key decisions
- Cache key = file stat fingerprint (probed before AND after the open): any append/rotation/truncate misses; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The memo returns shared immutable records (every consumer is read-only); one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Cold-boot cost is untouched by design — the remaining shell-boot work (config/providers/MCP/plugins) needs the lazy/parallel regime and stays measurable via the new stage lines.

{"content":"### What changed
- `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).
- Warm switches reuse the built context: `buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) in `ResumedContextCache`; an unchanged session file skips the projection walk entirely (`boot_stage context … source=cache` in fa.log).
- `JsonlSessionRepo.readCustomRecordsOfType` memoizes tail scans per (path, params, chain fingerprint) — the obligations-ledger/orphan-report/registry/steering rescans on every open/switch collapse to one stat each.
- Switches log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage — switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done, all naming the target sid — so regressions are attributable from fa.log alone.

### Key decisions
- Cache key = file stat fingerprint (probed before AND after the open): any append/rotation/truncate misses; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The memo returns shared immutable records (every consumer is read-only); one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Cold-boot cost is untouched by design — the remaining shell-boot work (config/providers/MCP/plugins) needs the lazy/parallel regime and stays measurable via the new stage lines.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/session_switch_boot_stages_test.dart \
  test/cli/session_switch_prompt_reuse_test.dart \
  test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart \
  test/session/custom_record_scan_memo_test.dart
```
Then `fa --session <big>` → `/sessions` → another session → back: the return switch logs `boot_stage context … source=cache`.

<details><summary>Switch pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SW[switch-begin] --> LOAD[open + walk]
  LOAD --> CTX{file unchanged since last open?}
  CTX -->|yes| REUSE[reuse built context]
  CTX -->|no| BUILD[buildContext + memoize]
  REUSE --> REH[rehydrate · memoized scan]
  BUILD --> REH
  REH --> REPLAY[replay] --> DONE[switch-done]
```

</details>

{"content":"### What changed
- `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).
- Warm switches reuse the built context: `buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) in `ResumedContextCache`; an unchanged session file skips the projection walk entirely (`boot_stage context … source=cache` in fa.log).
- `JsonlSessionRepo.readCustomRecordsOfType` memoizes tail scans per (path, params, chain fingerprint) — the obligations-ledger/orphan-report/registry/steering rescans on every open/switch collapse to one stat each.
- Switches log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage — switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done, all naming the target sid — so regressions are attributable from fa.log alone.

### Key decisions
- Cache key = file stat fingerprint (probed before AND after the open): any append/rotation/truncate misses; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The memo returns shared immutable records (every consumer is read-only); one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Cold-boot cost is untouched by design — the remaining shell-boot work (config/providers/MCP/plugins) needs the lazy/parallel regime and stays measurable via the new stage lines.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/session_switch_boot_stages_test.dart \
  test/cli/session_switch_prompt_reuse_test.dart \
  test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart \
  test/session/custom_record_scan_memo_test.dart
```
Then `fa --session <big>` → `/sessions` → another session → back: the return switch logs `boot_stage context … source=cache`.

<details><summary>Switch pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SW[switch-begin] --> LOAD[open + walk]
  LOAD --> CTX{file unchanged since last open?}
  CTX -->|yes| REUSE[reuse built context]
  CTX -->|no| BUILD[buildContext + memoize]
  REUSE --> REH[rehydrate · memoized scan]
  BUILD --> REH
  REH --> REPLAY[replay] --> DONE[switch-done]
```

</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}

Mid-REPL `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack and warm switches reuse the built context: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd differs, `Session.buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) and reused when the file is unchanged, and the repo's custom-record tail scans (obligations ledger, orphan reports, subagent registry, steering) are memoized per (path, params, fingerprint). - Context cache keys on the file's stat fingerprint (size+mtime, probed before and after the open) — any append/rotation invalidates it without write-barier machinery; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The context stage reports `source=cache` in fa.log so warm vs cold opens are attributable (gh-1734 AC: regressions attributable from the log).

### What changed
Mid-REPL `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack and warm switches reuse the built context: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd differs, `Session.buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) and reused when the file is unchanged, and the repo's custom-record tail scans (obligations ledger, orphan reports, subagent registry, steering) are memoized per (path, params, fingerprint). - `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).

{"content":"### What changed
- `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).
- Warm switches reuse the built context: `buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) in `ResumedContextCache`; an unchanged session file skips the projection walk entirely (`boot_stage context … source=cache` in fa.log).
- `JsonlSessionRepo.readCustomRecordsOfType` memoizes tail scans per (path, params, chain fingerprint) — the obligations-ledger/orphan-report/registry/steering rescans on every open/switch collapse to one stat each.
- Switches log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage — switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done, all naming the target sid — so regressions are attributable from fa.log alone.

### Key decisions
- Cache key = file stat fingerprint (probed before AND after the open): any append/rotation/truncate misses; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The memo returns shared immutable records (every consumer is read-only); one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Cold-boot cost is untouched by design — the remaining shell-boot work (config/providers/MCP/plugins) needs the lazy/parallel regime and stays measurable via the new stage lines.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/session_switch_boot_stages_test.dart \
  test/cli/session_switch_prompt_reuse_test.dart \
  test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart \

```
Then `fa --session <big>` → `/sessions` → another session → back: the return switch logs `boot_stage context … source=cache`.

<details><summary>Switch pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SW[switch-begin] --> LOAD[open + walk]

  CTX -->|yes| REUSE[reuse built context]
  CTX -->|no| BUILD[buildContext + memoize]
  REUSE --> REH[rehydrate · memoized scan]
  BUILD --> REH
  REH --> REPLAY[replay] --> DONE[switch-done]
```

</details>

{"content":"### What changed
- `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).
- Warm switches reuse the built context: `buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) in `ResumedContextCache`; an unchanged session file skips the projection walk entirely (`boot_stage context … source=cache` in fa.log).
- `JsonlSessionRepo.readCustomRecordsOfType` memoizes tail scans per (path, params, chain fingerprint) — the obligations-ledger/orphan-report/registry/steering rescans on every open/switch collapse to one stat each.
- Switches log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage — switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done, all naming the target sid — so regressions are attributable from fa.log alone.

### Key decisions
- Cache key = file stat fingerprint (probed before AND after the open): any append/rotation/truncate misses; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The memo returns shared immutable records (every consumer is read-only); one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Cold-boot cost is untouched by design — the remaining shell-boot work (config/providers/MCP/plugins) needs the lazy/parallel regime and stays measurable via the new stage lines.

### How to verify

{"content":"### What changed
- `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).
- Warm switches reuse the built context: `buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) in `ResumedContextCache`; an unchanged session file skips the projection walk entirely (`boot_stage context … source=cache` in fa.log).
- `JsonlSessionRepo.readCustomRecordsOfType` memoizes tail scans per (path, params, chain fingerprint) — the obligations-ledger/orphan-report/registry/steering rescans on every open/switch collapse to one stat each.
- Switches log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage — switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done, all naming the target sid — so regressions are attributable from fa.log alone.

### Key decisions
- Cache key = file stat fingerprint (probed before AND after the open): any append/rotation/truncate misses; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The memo returns shared immutable records (every consumer is read-only); one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Cold-boot cost is untouched by design — the remaining shell-boot work (config/providers/MCP/plugins) needs the lazy/parallel regime and stays measurable via the new stage lines.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/session_switch_boot_stages_test.dart \
  test/cli/session_switch_prompt_reuse_test.dart \
  test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart \
  test/session/custom_record_scan_memo_test.dart
```
Then `fa --session <big>` → `/sessions` → another session → back: the return switch logs `boot_stage context … source=cache`.

<details><summary>Switch pipeline</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SW[switch-begin] --> LOAD[open + walk]
  LOAD --> CTX{file unchanged since last open?}
  CTX -->|yes| REUSE[reuse built context]
  CTX -->|no| BUILD[buildContext + memoize]
  REUSE --> REH[rehydrate · memoized scan]
  BUILD --> REH
  REH --> REPLAY[replay] --> DONE[switch-done]
```

</details>

{"content":"### What changed
- `/sessions` switches no longer re-boot the shell stack: `_switchToMetadata` reloads skills/project context only when the adopted cwd actually differs (same project = the live prompt stays).
- Warm switches reuse the built context: `buildContext` results are cached per (session path, size+mtime) in `ResumedContextCache`; an unchanged session file skips the projection walk entirely (`boot_stage context … source=cache` in fa.log).
- `JsonlSessionRepo.readCustomRecordsOfType` memoizes tail scans per (path, params, chain fingerprint) — the obligations-ledger/orphan-report/registry/steering rescans on every open/switch collapse to one stat each.
- Switches log `boot_stage` lines covering every stage — switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done, all naming the target sid — so regressions are attributable from fa.log alone.

### Key decisions
- Cache key = file stat fingerprint (probed before AND after the open): any append/rotation/truncate misses; a stale probe can only miss, never serve stale bytes.
- The memo returns shared immutable records (every consumer is read-only); one entry per session path bounds memory.
- Cold-boot cost is untouched by design — the remaining shell-boot work (config/providers/MCP/plugins) needs the lazy/parallel regime and stays measurable via the new stage lines.

  REUSE --> REH[rehydrate · memoized scan]

The budget affects ensureCompactionBoundaryResident: with a bigger budget the walk may go FURTHER back (older records resident → the branch path extends further → context includes MORE history). With a smaller budget the walk stops earlier → the context is budget-truncated ("a valid budget-truncated resume").

In ONE process, when does the budget change between two loads of the same session? `_effectiveContextWindow` (model switch → /model changes the window), `_effectiveCompactionSettings.reserveTokens` (config), systemPrompt/tools (prompt recomposition — same cwd... a /skills reload could change the prompt size!). Actually, let me reconsider a potential problem in my warm-switch test flow: after `io.sendLine('/session $alphaId')` — `_switchSession(alphaId)` → `_sessionNameMatches(alphaId)` → exact id match → good.

Let me also think about whether the cache could serve a context built with a DIFFERENT system prompt (the parity budget) — the CONTEXT doesn't depend on the system prompt (buildContext projects records only; the budget only bounds the WALK residency). Two loads in the same process with different budgets: load 1 with prompt A walks to boundary X, builds context C1 (cached). Load 2 with prompt B (e.g., after a /model switch changing the window): walk goes to boundary Y≠X → buildContext would project a DIFFERENT branch slice — but my cache HIT serves C1! Hmm — is that a real hazard?

The budget affects ensureCompactionBoundaryResident: with a bigger budget the walk may go FURTHER back (older records resident → the branch path extends further → context includes MORE history). With a smaller budget the walk stops earlier → the context is budget-truncated ("a valid budget-truncated resume").

Let me also think about whether the cache could serve a context built with a DIFFERENT system prompt (the parity budget) — the CONTEXT doesn't depend on the system prompt (buildContext projects records only; the budget only bounds the WALK residency). Two loads in the same process with different budgets: load 1 with prompt A walks to boundary X, builds context C1 (cached). Load 2 with prompt B (e.g., after a /model switch changing the window): walk goes to boundary Y≠X → buildContext would project a DIFFERENT branch slice — but my cache HIT serves C1! Hmm — is that a real hazard?

The budget affects ensureCompactionBoundaryResident: with a bigger budget the walk may go FURTHER back (older records resident → the branch path extends further → context includes MORE history). With a smaller budget the walk stops earlier → the context is budget-truncated ("a valid budget-truncated resume").

In ONE process, when does the budget change between two loads of the same session? `_effectiveContextWindow` (model switch → /model changes the window), `_effectiveCompactionSettings.reserveTokens` (config), systemPrompt/tools (prompt recomposition — same cwd... a /skills reload could change the prompt size!). E.g.: boot on alpha (budget B1, context C1 cached) → user runs /model <bigger-window> → budget B2 > B1 → /session beta → /session alpha: my cache serves C1 — the B1-truncated context — while a fresh build under B2 would include MORE (or the same) history.

Is serving C1 WRONG? It's the same transcript, just possibly truncated differently at the OLD boundary. The session remains valid: the next auto-compaction... hmm, `buildContextMessages` (uncached) is used by the auto-compactor, which walks its own path. The context C1 is a budget-truncated valid resume. Marginal semantic drift: after switching to a LARGER window, a warm switch-back wouldn't pick up the extra history the larger window now allows (until the file changes). That's a minor staleness, not corruption — the transcript renders from `_agent.state.messages` (C1), and older history is reachable via scrollback paging.

But to be exact, I can make the cache key INCLUDE the budget fingerprint: `resumeParityBudget` returns an int (tokens). Key = (path, size, mtime, budget). Cheap: compute the budget BEFORE the fingerprint probe (it's pure arithmetic) and pass it into match/remember. That closes the drift completely. Let me do it — small change, closes a real (if minor) hole.

The budget affects ensureCompactionBoundaryResident: with a bigger budget the walk may go FURTHER back (older records resident → the branch path extends further → context includes MORE history). With a smaller budget the walk stops earlier → the context is budget-truncated ("a valid budget-truncated resume").

In ONE process, when does the budget change between two loads of the same session? `_effectiveContextWindow` (model switch → /model changes the window), `_effectiveCompactionSettings.reserveTokens` (config), systemPrompt/tools (prompt recomposition — same cwd... a /skills reload could change the prompt size!). The session remains valid: the next auto-compaction... hmm, `buildContextMessages` (uncached) is used by the auto-compactor, which walks its own path. The context C1 is a budget-truncated valid resume.
